note: Measured numbers behind assets/results.png. Every row is reproducible from the tools in this repository; see METHOD.md for how each was obtained and BENCHMARK.md for the DAVIS protocol.

reference.note: LocoTrack-B is the base this is fine-tuned from. Included because a fine-tune that quietly lost ground on the general benchmark would be worth knowing about; it did not.

occlusion.note: Synthetic occlusion benches with exact ground truth, 8 occluders each, built with tools/make_occlusion_bench.py --occluders 8 --seed N. Held out: the shipping checkpoint was selected on an earlier bench, before these three existed.
occlusion.metric: percentage of ground-truth-occluded frames placed within 5 px

confidence.note: The model's own per-frame confidence used as a detector for its own >5 px frames.

localisation.note: Synthetic bench, exact homography ground truth, 600 tracks, raw neural output with no refinement stage.

scoring_note: tools/score_occlusion.py now excludes samples whose ground truth has left the plate (a point outside the picture cannot be tracked) and can score raw model output ungated via --npz. Neither change alters the rows in this file: the occluded within-5px figures were re-measured with the exclusion and move by at most 0.7 points (occ11 73.9->74.6, occ12 63.0->63.1, occ13 62.1->62.6), all slightly favourable. The exclusion does matter for maxima and means, which are order statistics -- on one bench it moved the worst visible error from 389.30 px to 16.86 px. See COMPARISON.md.

davis_384x512.note: Same checkpoint at 384x512 instead of 256x256, strided. Read with the protocol in mind: TAP-Vid resizes every clip to 256x256 before the model sees it, so this upscales an already-downsampled frame and there is no extra detail to recover. The gain comes from the model's internal refinement ladder, not from more pixels -- which is why DAVIS moves about a point while plate-resolution benches halve. DAVIS cannot measure the resolution question; see COMPARISON.md.
davis_384x512.cost: occlusion accuracy falls 1.9 points. The model commits a position where it previously abstained; on the occlusion benches those positions are right, but OA is the metric for knowing when to keep quiet, and this is a real trade.

cost_on_a_real_4k_shot.note: 312 frames of 3840x2160 decoded to 960 wide, 400 seeds, one 16 GB RTX A4000. Recorded because the resolution recommendation is only useful if it fits.
cost_on_a_real_4k_shot.headroom: 12.22 GB of 16, and it does NOT scale with track count -- measured flat to the last decimal from 400 to 3025 seeds on the same shot (12.22 GB throughout, while s/frame went 0.040 -> 0.182). An earlier version of this field said to check headroom at your own seed count; that was wrong. VRAM is bounded on both axes: query_chunk_size (64) bounds the track dimension and the engine's auto-window caps the temporal window at 120 frames at 384x512 and 250 at 256x256, so a longer clip is windowed rather than held whole. 12.22 GB is one window of feature volume.

vram_vs_seed_count.note: peak GB at 384x512 on a 312-frame 3840x2160 shot, uniform grid seeding

stage_c_training.note: Four training runs, each one flag from its neighbour, 20,000 steps at accumulation 16 with a cosine decay. Scored on the same four synthetic occlusion benches with the same 600 seeds as every other number here.

what_each_run_isolated.c1: the schedule and batch alone -- frozen mixer, historical occluded weight
what_each_run_isolated.c2: + the vendor's temporal transformer made trainable
what_each_run_isolated.c3: + the occluded position term normalised to a stated 0.2 SHARE
what_each_run_isolated.c4: + trained at the higher feature ladder (384)

at_256x256_vs_shipping.note: mean over 4 benches, ungated, truth on plate. Negative is better.

stage_c_training.headline: worst-case visible error 21.94 -> 13.30 px (-39%), occluded 4.36 -> 3.62 px (-17%), and re-acquisition improved rather than being traded away.

davis_check.note: The generalisation gate. Stage C trained hard on MOVi-E, so the point of keeping a public benchmark in the loop is to catch a model that improved on the synthetic benches by overfitting to them.
davis_check.reading: c3 is unchanged on DAVIS, so its bench gains are not overfitting. c4 is the best model measured here and repairs the occlusion-accuracy regression that running at 384 introduced -- 88.0 -> 90.5, past the 256 baseline of 89.9.

stage_c_training.which_to_use: No single checkpoint wins everything, and saying otherwise would mean choosing the metric after seeing the results. jefftracker_occ.ckpt (c3) for occluded accuracy; jefftracker_occ_ladder384.ckpt (c4) for occlusion classification and DAVIS; the original inf_s4000.ckpt is marginally best on plain visible accuracy at matched coverage.
